object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A consignment of goods that is tracked through the logistics network.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to each shipment for tracking purposes.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A physical item or good that can be included in shipments.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity. Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: SKU
object_types.definition: Stock Keeping Unit; the unique identifier for a product.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU. For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The number of units of a product contained in a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity.

object_types.name: Warehouse
object_types.definition: A physical storage facility where shipments can be held.

source_references.excerpt: Warehouses have a warehouse code.

object_types.name: WarehouseCode
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a warehouse.

ambiguities.description: Shipment identification: The transcript refers to 'shipment S-100' as an example, suggesting ShipmentNumber is the identifier. However, it is not explicitly stated whether ShipmentNumber is the only identifier or whether Shipment might also be identified by other attributes (e.g., creation date, origin warehouse). Clarification needed: Is ShipmentNumber the sole unique identifier, or are there alternate or composite identification schemes?

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.

ambiguities.description: Warehouse assignment and Shipment assignment relationship: The model treats 'Shipment sits in Warehouse' as a many-to-many relationship with the frequency constraint (1 to 2 warehouses per shipment). However, it is unclear whether a Warehouse can hold zero shipments, multiple shipments, or whether there are other constraints on warehouse capacity or assignment logic. Clarification needed: What is the minimum participation of Warehouse in the 'sits in' relationship? Can a Warehouse be empty, or must it always hold at least one Shipment?

source_references.excerpt: A shipment can be split across warehouses -- up to three warehouses per shipment. [...] a shipment sits in at most two warehouses now.

ambiguities.description: Product-Shipment relationship optionality: The model requires every Shipment to contain at least one Product (implied by the frequency constraint on the ternary fact type), but this is not explicitly stated. It is unclear whether an empty shipment (containing no products) is valid or whether the transcript assumes all shipments always contain products. Clarification needed: Can a Shipment exist without any products, or must every Shipment contain at least one Product-Quantity combination?

ambiguities.description: Policy change timing: The transcript records a policy change from 'up to three warehouses' to 'at most two warehouses' that occurred last quarter. It is unclear whether this is a historical fact (legacy shipments may follow the old rule) or whether the constraint should apply uniformly to all shipments (including retroactively). Clarification needed: Should the two-warehouse maximum apply to all shipments in the system, or only to new shipments created after the policy change?
